paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. Hezekiah got a hard word from the LORD, and he didn't go quiet. He turned his face to the wall and prayed, and he wept bitterly (Isaiah 38:2-3). Then the LORD answered: "I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears." (Isaiah 38:5) You can bring God the real stuff, the tears and the shaky voice and all. I know a little about lying in the dark and not knowing what comes next, and a worn-out stamper like me is glad somebody listens.

Now look at what Hezekiah does with his fifteen extra years. He doesn't just say thanks and move on. He writes it all down, even the ugly part where he thought he'd never see the LORD in the land of the living (Isaiah 38:11). Then he says, "Your love has delivered me from the pit of oblivion, for You have cast all my sins behind Your back." (Isaiah 38:17) That's a king who knows he was rescued by love, and his sins are put behind God's back. Nobody earns that, friend, and I'm still amazed by it.

So what's a baker supposed to do with this? Do what Hezekiah did: "The living, only the living, can thank You, as I do today; fathers will tell their children about Your faithfulness." (Isaiah 38:19) Every day you're breathing is a day to thank Him and to tell somebody how faithful He's been. Pray when it's heavy, praise when it's lifted, and pass the story on. And stay close, because this king's story isn't over yet.
